dwelling_habits.dwelling: Coral reefs and wreck edges from snorkel depths to deeper drop-offs.
dwelling_habits.food: Sponges, tunicates, and algae picked from the reef.
dwelling_habits.feeding: Pairs patrol a territory, nipping sponges that other fish ignore.
dwelling_habits.mating: Usually close pairs that swim flank to flank.
dwelling_habits.socializing: Juveniles are bold black-and-yellow cleaners; adults stay close as a duo.

fun_facts: Young French angels run tiny cleaning stations — a spa day for bigger fish.
Yellow bars fade as they grow into elegant black-and-gold adults.

dwelling_habits.dwelling: Aruba reef edges, mangrove channels, and sandy patches near coral heads.
dwelling_habits.food: Small crustaceans and worms taken from sand at night.
dwelling_habits.feeding: Daytime schools hover over the reef; nighttime they fan out to forage.
dwelling_habits.mating: Spawns in groups; larvae settle back to shallow nurseries.
dwelling_habits.socializing: Classic yellow-striped schools — a staple snorkel sight around the ABC islands.

fun_facts: Named for the grunting sounds they make with teeth and swim bladder.
Often share daytime hangouts with other grunt species over the same coral head.
